key_idea: Convert Peluse's inverse theorem into a structural decomposition of the dual function using Hahn–Banach, so that Ionescu–Wainger major-arc projections remove the structured part. Then upgrade from ℓ^∞ to ℓ^2 control with ℓ^p-improving bounds and from local to global support with Schur-test almost-orthogonality.
reason: The excerpt follows a clear strategy: an inverse theorem, then dualization, then a series of upgrades. The Hahn–Banach dual-function decomposition is a well-chosen and reusable idea, but it is standard in additive combinatorics. Its force is spread over a chain of corollaries that each patch one technical shortcoming (ℓ^1 errors, ℓ^∞ control, support), and these rely on interpolation and estimate bookkeeping, so the proof is competent and fairly clean rather than striking.
recognized: Krause–Mirek–Peluse–Wright style / Krause–Mirek–Tao, 'Pointwise ergodic theorems for non-conventional bilinear polynomial averages' (Annals), Section 6 minor/major arc inverse-theorem step
